title: Lamps on the Lagoon
logline: Lamps are lit on the water at dusk. Through the night, fish and insects gather to the light, and a crew works the same patient rhythm they have worked for years, hoping this catch is enough.
human_question: What does a whole night of patient, repeated effort feel like when the result is still not known?

premise.story: A night of lamp fishing on a lagoon: the lighting of the lamps, the long watch, the steady, repetitive work of the catch, and the crew's own account of what a good night and a bad night mean for their households.
premise.place: A lagoon at night, lamps the only light on the water.
premise.experience: The viewer sits through the long, quiet hours of the watch, lit only by lamplight and stars, and feels the weight of a livelihood that depends on this same night repeating itself, well or badly, again and again.

concept_links.why: Ageing, illness, loss and simply not getting what is wanted or needed are named among the ordinary occasions for this state of mind [C007-P:L49]. A night's fishing is one livelihood's version of that: the crew cannot control what the water gives, and a bad night carries a real, quiet worry about what follows it.

Restlessness, a mind that will not settle on what is in front of it, is one of the four factors present in every state of this kind [C022-P:L73; C022-M:L19]. The long, watchful hours of a night's fishing are offered here only as an image of sustained, unsettled attention under uncertainty, not as a moral reading of the crew themselves.

what_camera_could_observe: Lamps being prepared and lit as dusk falls
Insects and fish gathering to the light through the night
The crew's patient, repeated work: watching, drawing in, sorting
Quiet exchanges between crew members through the long hours
The catch at dawn, and what it means for the crew that night
what_must_be_real: The crew, their methods and their night's catch must be entirely genuine and unscripted. Nothing about the crew's effort or patience should be narrated as a lesson about their character; the image of light and gathering life belongs to the source text, never to the people shown.

possible_arc.opening: Dusk, lamps carried out onto still water.
possible_arc.turn: The long middle of the night: rhythm, quiet, uncertainty.
possible_arc.ending_open: Whatever dawn actually brings, good or lean, ends the film in the crew's own words.

requirements: A lagoon community that still practises lamp fishing at night
A crew willing to be filmed across a full night's work
Safe camera positions on or near the water after dark

risks: Turning a livelihood into a visual allegory that frames the crew unfairly
Long, slow night footage losing narrative shape without a clear human stake
Safety on the water after dark for crew and film team
drop_if: No lamp-fishing crew can be found willing to be filmed for a full night
The method is no longer practised in a findable, accessible community

connections.note: Two night vigils at the edge of water and wild: one guarding land from what comes to take it, one drawing life toward a light.
Two coastal, water-based livelihoods: one marked by conflict and repair, one carried by patient, repeated work.
